system.name: Melange Demographic Potential and district metrics
system.description: District and state CU market-opportunity scores: v2.1 growth room (location quotients and shift-share) and v3.0 CU footprint (the default). Includes the Census congressional-district metric build. Not wired to the Demo% pillar input.

components.name: Demographic Potential v2.1 (growth room)
components.computes: 0-100 score = 100 x sum(weight x percentile) over LQ strength 20, competitive shift 20, aligned sectors 15, branch whitespace 15, deposit whitespace 5, LMI 10, large employer 8, small business 7.
components.method: LQ = local share / US share; shift-share identity. Qualification LQ >= 1.25. Non-default.
empirical_questions: Does growth-room score predict subsequent CU membership or branch growth in a district?
components.heading: Demographic Potential v2.1 (growth room)

components.name: Demographic Potential v3.0 (CU footprint, default)
components.computes: Score from CU employment LQ .30, establishment LQ .20, branch share .25 and deposit share .25; qualifies at employment LQ >= 1.0.
components.method: Default since 2026-09-16 (D-035). Opposite direction to v2.1.
assumptions: Current footprint is the potential (owner ruling)
empirical_questions: Is a district's CU footprint associated with its members' CU-aligned behaviour (constituency interest)?
components.heading: Demographic Potential v3.0 (CU footprint, default)

components.name: Census congressional-district metrics
components.computes: 489 rows x 25 ACS and CBP metrics at state and district level.
components.method: Census API pulls stacked across levels. Documented boundary mismatch: ACS on 119th-Congress districts, CBP on 116th.
empirical_questions: How large is measurement error from the CBP-ACS boundary mismatch for redistricted states?
components.heading: Census congressional-district metrics

evidence.title: Learnable Skills, or Unteachable Instinct? What Can and What Cannot Be Taught in the Lobbying Profession
evidence.claim: Relationship targeting means finding lawmakers who respond to information and who have an electoral interest in the group's constituency (p.18). Lobbyists should pick out lawmakers with a relevant interest (p.17).
evidence.system_side: The default footprint mode scores a district's existing CU footprint (employment LQ, establishments, branches, deposits) and qualifies a district at employment LQ >= 1.0. Paul's ruling: 'the footprint should be the potential'. The weights are labelled judgmental and unestimated.
evidence.transfer: This matches the targeting logic only in concept: aim at members whose constituents hold a stake. The paper does not test whether that stake predicts responsiveness, and Demographic Potential does not feed Demo%. No weight support.

evidence.title: The Effects of Firms' Lobbying on Resource Misallocation
evidence.claim: Firm-politician connection is defined as politicians representing the firm's headquarters state. The paper reports no headquarters moves in its data, and the likelihood that a politician changes district is less than 1 percent. The instrument built on the home-state link has first-stage F 14.30 and 13.10 (Table 2).
evidence.system_side: Footprint v3.0 (the default) scores districts by employment LQ 0.30, establishment LQ 0.20, CU branch share 0.25 and CU deposit share 0.25. A district qualifies at unrounded employment LQ of at least 1.0. It does not feed Demo percent (not checked).
evidence.transfer: In H&K the home-state link is an identifying assumption for headquarters only, not an estimated effect of employment or branch footprint, and it is at state level, not district level. It gives weak support to the state-layer idea. It does not validate the footprint weights or any claim that footprint predicts CU-aligned behaviour.

evidence.title: Do Redistricting Commissions Avoid Partisan Gerrymanders?
evidence.claim: Redistricting materially reshuffles how voters are distributed across districts: the SD and skew of district vote shares differ from neutral by several points. The authors also flag boundary-vintage mismatch (VTD shapefiles out of date because states re-precinct more often than they redistrict) as a limitation on their own estimates.
evidence.system_side: The Census CD scraper stacks ACS metrics on 119th-Congress districts with 2020 CBP establishment counts on 116th-Congress district boundaries. The mismatch is documented and accepted as tolerable.
evidence.transfer: The paper is about vote distributions, not business counts. It does not quantify measurement error from mixing boundary vintages. It only reinforces that boundary changes are not innocuous in states that redrew substantially, which includes the 2020-round redraws and the later mid-decade redraws. The paper offers no evidence about how large the CBP error is.

evidence.title: Characterizing equitable access to grocery stores during disasters using location-based data
evidence.claim: How many facilities a zone has is a poor indicator of realized access. Correlation of stores per zone with the preparation-phase % change: stores visited r = -0.06 (p = 0.007), trip time r = -0.01 (p = 0.448), trip distance r = -0.03 (p = 0.100). Window: 24 Aug 2017. Denominator: Harris County zones in the analysis, N not reported. Food-desert status alone did not separate high- from low-income access.
evidence.system_side: The default Demographic Potential (footprint, ruling R7, D-035) scores a district on supply-side presence. Weights: CU employment LQ .30, establishment LQ .20, CU branch share .25, CU deposit share .25. It treats current footprint as the potential and makes no use-based or access-based measure.
evidence.transfer: Weak analogy only. The paper covers grocery trips in a disaster in one county, with access measured from mobility traces. Demographic Potential is a national, district-level market score under normal conditions. It is explicitly not a measure of support or access, and the footprint choice is an owner ruling. The paper's lesson (supply counts are not realized use) would matter only if footprint were read as members' or constituents' access to CUs. It does not challenge the owner's choice to treat footprint as potential. The same caution applies to the growth_room branch-whitespace term (demographic_potential.py:152).

evidence.title: The Gameability of Redistricting Criteria
evidence.claim: On the 10x9 grid, Plan 2 has the best People Change (9.5 percent, tied with Plan 3) but the second-worst Area Change (13.3 percent; Plan 1 is best at 7.8 percent). People, Area and Precinct Change first match each new district to an old one; Fowlkes-Mallows and Variation of Information are matching-free. The county-split measures in Table 1 disagree on the best plan (fewest counties split is Plan 2 with 1; lowest Shannon entropy is Plan 3 at 1.265; lowest Even Splits is Plan 4 at 2.485).
evidence.system_side: census_cd_scraper.R sets ACS_YEAR 2024 (119th-Congress districts) and CBP_YEAR 2020 (116th-Congress CD boundaries) and notes a few new CDs are NA. redistricting_density.py weights counties by blocks-in-district over blocks-in-county (its receipt says the BEF file has no population weights), reports split_county_count, sets seat_changed = int(seat_117 != seat_119) from district labels, and also computes cu_share_old, cu_share_new and delta per member.
evidence.transfer: Measurement design transfers. A per-state matching-based or matching-free change measure on CD116 vs CD119 block assignments could size the CBP-ACS vintage error and could replace the label-only flag. Limits: the paper works in precinct or ward units on population, the system weights blocks, and the paper does not say which basis is right. Descriptive only, tested only on Minnesota and Wisconsin.

evidence.title: Simulated redistricting plans for the analysis and evaluation of redistricting in the United States
evidence.claim: VEST precinct returns are estimated down to 2010 blocks and crosswalked to 2020 blocks, then aggregated to any district plan. Each state's output is a redist_map object plus 5,000 plans: 1,000 precincts x 5 districts x 5,001 plans gives 25,005 rows (p.3-5).
evidence.system_side: The scraper pulls ACS 2024 1-year on 119th-Congress districts and CBP 2020 on 116th-Congress districts and stacks them. Some new districts come back NA. The boundary mismatch is documented but never quantified.
evidence.transfer: The block-crosswalk recipe could re-aggregate county or ZIP CBP counts onto 119th boundaries, but only with population-weighted allocation. That allocation adds its own error, because establishments are not distributed like population. The paper reports no estimate of that error, so it gives a method only, not an answer to the component's question about measurement error.
